newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed's Augustine to retire as CEO.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed's Augustine to retire as CEO.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp. said Friday that Norman Augustine will retire as chief executive later this year to pursue outside interests but will remain chairman of the board.
Vance Coffman, currently president and chief operating officer, will assume the additional post of chief executive officer as of Aug. 1.
Augustine, an architect of the Lockheed-Martin Marietta merger, has served as the company's chief executive since January 1996, the company said.
Coffman, 53, previously served as president of Lockheed's space and strategic missiles sector.
The company also said Peter Teets, presently chief operating officer of its information and services sector, will become executive vice president and chief operating officer of the corporation.
The Bethesda, Md.-based defence company said Augustine's retirement was "in keeping with his longstanding plans."
It said Augustine, 61, plans to focus on education and public service after retirement, and will join the faculty at Princeton University in the fall.

"Norm has been the corporate strategist, laying down the overall direction in the merger and acquisition end of things, but he has not done the operational stuff," said Bankers Trust analyst Wolfgang Demisch.

"Now the corporate structure is set and for the next few years the challenge is day-to-day execution at the kind of profit that investors expect," Demisch said. "Coffman has done this repeatedly and with great success."
Cai von Rumohr, an analyst with Cowen & Co., agreed.
"Coffman is a good solid operating manager while Augustine was really the architect, the visionary of the consolidation," von Rumohr said.
Augustine is credited with assembling former Martin Marietta into a satellite and rocket giant, culminating in the 1995 merger with Lockheed Corp.
"Now that the pieces are together, its more of a case of operating, so having an operating guy as the CEO makes sense."
Lockheed's stock rose 62.5 cents to $84.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
